Diagnostics in persephone3

Source: vignettes/persephone-diagnostics.Rmd
persephone-diagnostics.Rmd

Introduction

diagnosticsTable() collects the most important diagnostic statistics of a seasonal adjustment object (created with perX13() or perTramo()) into a single data frame. Most of its columns are passed through directly from the JDemetra+ output — persephone3 requests a fixed set of user-defined items (see userdefined_default in the package code) and reads them from the Java result object.

This vignette documents how individual fields of that table are computed. Currently it covers the overall quality summary (TotalQ); further fields will be documented here as the diagnostics table evolves.

The TotalQ field

TotalQ is the value of the JDemetra+ output node quality.summary. It is not computed in R: the R side only reads the node from the Java result and reports it unchanged. A common misconception is that TotalQ is based on the M-statistics Q and Q2 alone — in fact, Q and Q2 are just two of many tests that feed into it (and, for TRAMO/SEATS, they are not involved at all).

The computation happens in the JDemetra+ output extractors (X13Extractor.java and TramoSeatsExtractor.java, which work identically) in two steps:

Step 1: Classify each individual test

A fixed list of diagnostic test groups is evaluated, and each individual test is classified into one of the quality levels Good, Uncertain, Bad or Severe (see X13Factory.java and TramoSeatsFactory.java for the default lists):

Test group X-13 TRAMO/SEATS
Coherence of the decomposition (SA vs. components) yes yes
Residual tests (Ljung-Box, normality, …) yes yes
Out-of-sample / forecasting tests yes yes
Outliers yes yes
Spectral test (residual seasonality at seasonal frequencies) yes yes
Combined seasonality tests yes yes
Advanced residual seasonality tests yes yes
Residual trading day tests yes yes
M-statistics summary Q and Q2 yes no
Wiener-Kolmogorov diagnostics no yes

The two method-specific groups use the following thresholds:

  • X-13 M-statistics (MDiagnostics.java): Q and Q2 are not p-values but already quality scores — the proportion of the M-statistics exceeding their critical value (Q2 excludes M7 from the computation). They are classified directly by value:
    • Q >= 2 → Severe, Q >= 1 → Bad, otherwise Good
    • the same rule for Q2
  • SEATS Wiener-Kolmogorov tests (SeatsDiagnostics.java): genuine p-values (variance of the seasonal component, variance of the irregular component, and their correlation):
    • p <= 0.005 → Bad, p > 0.05 → Good, otherwise Uncertain

Step 2: Aggregate to an overall quality

The classification of all individual tests is combined by ProcDiagnostic.summary() (ProcDiagnostic.java):

  1. If any test is Error, the overall result is Error. Otherwise, if any test is Severe, the overall result is Severe.
  2. Otherwise the mean score over all interpretable tests is formed, with Good = 3, Uncertain = 2, Bad = 0:
    • mean >= 2.5 → Good
    • mean >= 1.5 → Uncertain
    • otherwise → Bad
  3. If no test is interpretable, the result is Undefined.

The resulting string (Good, Uncertain, Bad, Severe, Undefined or Error) is what quality.summary — and hence the TotalQ column — contains.

Note that TotalQ reflects the model as a whole. It can change when the regression model changes even if the individual values of Q and Q2 move only slightly, because the classification of many tests contributes to the average. Conversely, a single Severe test (for example a strong residual trading day effect) is enough to make the overall summary Severe.

Example 

library(persephone3)

obj <- perX13(AirPassengers, "rsa3")
obj$run()

diagnosticsTable(obj)[, c("Q", "Q2", "TotalQ")]

With the default thresholds, Q and Q2 values well below 1 (as is typical for a clean multiplicative series like AirPassengers) are classified as Good on their own, and if the other diagnostic groups are also unproblematic, the overall summary TotalQ is Good as well.

  • JDemetra+ v3 source, jdplus-main: X13Extractor, TramoSeatsExtractor, ProcDiagnostic, MDiagnostics, SeatsDiagnostics
